q: SEVOTTAM is a…
o: Quality management system for public services
x: Seva + uttam = excellent service. It is a quality management framework.

q: Which committee is NOT about civil services?
x: Balwant Rai Mehta (1957) was about Panchayati Raj.

q: The Santhanam Committee on corruption was set up in…
x: Set up in 1962, report in 1964. It led to the Central Vigilance Commission (1964).

q: The Royal Commission on the Superior Civil Services in India is better known as the…
x: The Lee Commission (1923–24) led to the first Public Service Commission in 1926.

q: The Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA) was set up in…
x: New Delhi, 1954, on Paul Appleby's advice.

q: The Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy was first set up in 1948 at…
x: Started at Mount Abu in 1948; moved to Hyderabad in 1975.

q: Where is the National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj (NIRDPR)?
x: Hyderabad, under the Ministry of Rural Development.

q: "Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance" was the first report of the…
x: The 2nd ARC's first report (2006).

q: The well-known list of 27 modes of corruption is credited to the…
x: Many tick Santhanam because the names appear together, but the list is credited to the CVC.

q: Which is the most effective means of citizens' control over administration?
x: Most keys choose election, because voters can remove a government.

q: The British idea of political neutrality of civil servants came from the…
x: Masterman (1949) = neutral. Northcote–Trevelyan = merit. Fulton = specialists.

q: Which is a tool of EXECUTIVE control over administration?
x: Audit reports go to Parliament, so audit is legislative control.

q: The Public Accounts Committee is a tool of…
x: Parliament's committees, Question Hour and CAG reports are legislative control.

q: Which Charter Act ended selection of civil servants by favour and began open competition?
x: 1853. The Macaulay Committee (1854) then designed the exam; the first was held in London in 1855.

q: Who opened Fort William College in 1800 to train young officers?
x: Lord Wellesley, at Calcutta.

q: Which commission divided services into Imperial, Provincial and Subordinate?
x: The Aitchison Commission (1886).

q: The Islington Commission (1912) asked for…
o: Separation of revenue and court work
x: It recommended more Indians in the higher services.

q: Which law created Federal and Provincial Public Service Commissions?
x: The 1935 Act. In 1950 the Federal PSC became the UPSC.

q: Which is NOT an All India Service?
x: The three All India Services: IAS, IPS and the Indian Forest Service (1966). IFS (Foreign) is a central service.

q: The Indian Forest Service became an All India Service in…
Which committee added the essay paper to the civil services exam?
x: Satish Chandra (1989) reviewed the exam and added the essay.

q: The Baswan Committee (2016) studied…
o: Civil services exam age and pattern
x: It reviewed eligibility, age and the exam pattern.

q: The Yugandhar Committee (2003) dealt with…
x: Yugandhar = mid-career training. Surinder Nath = appraisal. Hota = reforms.

q: Which British report first proposed a permanent civil service chosen by merit through an exam?
x: Northcote–Trevelyan (1854) = merit.

q: The Fulton Committee (1968) in Britain criticised…
x: Fulton wanted more specialists and training.

q: LBSNAA, which trains IAS officers, is located at…
x: Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration, Mussoorie (1959).

q: The Indira Gandhi National Forest Academy is in…
x: Dehradun; it trains Indian Forest Service officers.

q: Which institute trains Odisha's state civil service officers?
o: State Institute of Rural Development, Sambalpur
x: Gopabandhu Academy of Administration, Bhubaneswar.

q: The RTI movement began with which organisation in Rajasthan?
x: In the 1990s MKSS asked to see how village money was spent.

q: The RTI Act came into force on…
x: Passed in June 2005, in force on 12 October 2005.

q: Which section of the RTI Act requires offices to publish information on their own?
x: Section 4: proactive disclosure. Section 8: exemptions.

q: Which section of the RTI Act lists information that need not be given?
x: Section 8 lists exemptions such as security and privacy.

q: Under RTI, the second appeal goes to the…
x: First appeal to a senior officer; second to the Central or State Information Commission.

q: India adopted the Citizens' Charter in…
x: Britain started it in 1991; India adopted it in 1997.

q: Public grievances can be filed online on…
x: Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System.

q: The Vohra Committee (1993) studied…
o: Links between criminals, politicians and officers
x: Its report described the criminal–politician–officer nexus.

q: Since 2018 amendments, the Prevention of Corruption Act also makes it a crime to…
x: Bribe-giving became a separate offence in 2018.

q: Which commission first suggested Lokpal and Lokayukta?
x: The 1st ARC (1966).

q: How many reports did the 2nd Administrative Reforms Commission give?
x: 15 reports; the 4th was Ethics in Governance, the 12th Citizen Centric Administration.

q: "Citizen Centric Administration" was the 12th report of the…
x: 2nd Administrative Reforms Commission.

q: The Rajamannar Committee (1969) on Centre–State relations was set up by…
x: Tamil Nadu set it up.

q: Which commission took a second look at Centre–State relations in 2007?
x: Punchhi (2007, report 2010).

q: The Sarkaria Commission recommended setting up a…
x: The Inter-State Council (Article 263) was set up in 1990.

q: The National Informatics Centre (NIC) was set up in…
x: NIC (1976) brought computers into government offices.

q: The National e-Governance Plan was launched in…
x: NeGP (2006) put services like passports and income tax online.

q: Which is NOT one of the three aims of Digital India?
x: The three aims: infrastructure, services on demand, digital empowerment.

q: Aadhaar is a…
x: 12 digits, linked to fingerprints and iris.

q: Which platform is an online locker for certificates?
x: DigiLocker stores digital documents.

q: Government offices buy goods and services on…
x: Government e-Marketplace.

q: BHASHINI is a…
x: BHASHINI translates between Indian languages using AI.

q: iGOT Karmayogi is linked to…
x: Mission Karmayogi (2020).

q: UMANG is…
o: One app for many government services
x: Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance.

q: The 28th National Conference on e-Governance (2025) was held at…
x: Visakhapatnam, September 2025.

q: The theme "Technology for Accelerating Development" belongs to the…
x: Asked in 2018.

q: Bhulekh in Odisha is a portal for…
x: Bhulekh = land records online. SAMS = college admission. Odisha One = single portal.

q: SAMS in Odisha is used for…
x: Student Academic Management System; won a national award in 2026.

q: Odisha passed its Right to Public Services Act in…
x: Odisha Right to Public Services Act, 2012.

q: Lord Cornwallis separated which two kinds of work in the civil service?
x: He paid officers well and separated revenue from judicial work.
